ticks.git: Ticks does not issue or persist execution credentials. Ordinary Git/SSH authentication for a human checkout remains Git's own credential helper or agent; ticfac owns source access for jobs.

schema.$comment: The ~/.ticfacrc key/value shape, written in the STRICT SUBSET both readers validate with — internal/tkcontract/schema.go and cloud/factory/test/json-schema.ts. Until bundle 3.0.0 this block used oneOf, const, minLength, format and pattern, none of which either validator implements: both sides hand-rolled a partial reader for it, both ignored the keywords they did not handle, and `format: uri` meant something different in Go (url.ParseRequestURI) than in TypeScript (new URL). A schema that reads as if it constrained something no validator checks is the exact failure contracts/README.md warns about, so the constraints the subset cannot enforce are now DESCRIPTIONS — a claim a reader makes about the value, not a claim a validator silently drops. Growing the subset is a code change on both sides, on purpose.

factory_url.description: Absolute https URL of the deployed factory Worker.

factory_token.description: The factory bearer token. Non-empty; the Worker stores only its hash.

factory_version.description: The factory version this laptop last deployed, e.g. 0.31.0.

factory_github_token.description: GitHub installation or personal access token. Non-empty.

factory_github_login.description: The GitHub login the token authenticates as. Non-empty.

factory_github_repo.description: owner/repo, with no whitespace and exactly one slash.

factory_github_token_expires_at.description: RFC3339 instant, or the empty string when the token does not expire. Empty and absent are different claims: absent means setup never reached this rung.

factory_github_refresh_token_expires_at.description: RFC3339 instant, or the empty string when the refresh token does not expire.

factory_gateway_url.description: Absolute AI Gateway URL the Worker routes model calls through.

factory_gateway_provider.description: Which provider the gateway passes through to. `workers-ai` is native inference and the only one the Cloudflare credit covers.

factory_gateway_key.description: The provider key. May be empty for workers-ai, which needs none.

factory_cloudflare_api_token.description: Cloudflare API token used for gateway telemetry and billing reads. Non-empty.

factory_workers_ai_billing_mode.description: Which Workers AI billing shape this account is on.

invalid.$comment: Appendix to `schema` above. Until bundle 3.0.0 this contract had NO negative example at all: both readers walked valid_example against a hand-rolled partial reader, so nothing had ever watched the schema refuse a document. A validator nobody has seen refuse anything is not known to refuse anything, and every one of these pins the refusal it expects — a negative that only proves 'something failed' is satisfied by a validator that has quietly stopped checking the thing the case was written about.
invalid.name: an unknown factory_ key
invalid.why: additionalProperties is false because a misspelled key is a credential the operator BELIEVES they set. A typo that silently persists is the whole reason the file's shape is closed.

invalid.name: a value that is not a string
invalid.why: the file is line-oriented key=value, so every value is text. A number here means something upstream wrote a parsed JSON object where the reader expects a rendered line, and a token that arrives as a number is a token nothing can send.

invalid.name: a gateway provider outside the closed set
invalid.why: the provider decides which credential is even needed and who is billed — workers-ai is native inference the Cloudflare credit covers, everything else is cash through the gateway. An unrecognised provider routes a run at a vendor nobody chose.
invalid.expect_error_contains: $.factory_gateway_provider: gemini is not one of the permitted values [workers-ai anthropic openai openrouter]

invalid.name: a github auth rung the ladder does not have
invalid.why: factory_github_auth records WHICH rung produced the token, which is what tells a refresh path whether there is a refresh token to use at all. A third value is a rung with no code behind it.
invalid.expect_error_contains: $.factory_github_auth: oauth-app is not one of the permitted values [device-flow pat]

invalid.name: a billing mode outside the closed set
invalid.why: the billing mode decides where a run's cost is reconciled. `.tick/learnings.md`: ~$50 of Workers AI spend once appeared in no billing page, so a mode nothing implements is a run whose cost has no home.
invalid.expect_error_contains: $.factory_workers_ai_billing_mode: prepaid is not one of the permitted values [postpaid unified]

stop.rule: A stop is a durable refusal to issue credentials, not a revocation a restart can undo.

metered.unknown_cost: refuse when a cost budget is configured

steps: Load ~/.ticfacrc and scan ~/.ticksrc for assignment lines whose key starts with factory_.
Copy only values absent from ~/.ticfacrc, preserving the destination value if it already exists.
Atomically save ~/.ticfacrc at 0600 before atomically rewriting ~/.ticksrc without factory_ lines; preserve all other lines.
Emit one stderr notice only when values were copied; no notice on a no-op or a resumed drain.
migration.crash_safety: If the process dies after destination save and before source drain, the next invocation sees destination values and only drains the old lines; it never overwrites a newer destination value.
migration.retention: Read the legacy shape indefinitely by default; remove that compatibility path only in a later explicit decision.
